baselineRegression.method: Identical final tests against isolated turn-start copies of both components and their original legalToolClient; live source never reverted

diffCheck: passed with repository CRLF whitespace settings
preserved: Contract review retains its dedicated endpoint and 10000-character submission limit; bid generation retains its legal tool route and case-persistence arguments.
Existing backend authentication, organization role rules, execution and persistence logic unchanged.
Risk parsing uses the existing production parser, derives only from successful output and discards an old selected risk when results change.
Case metadata and language refreshes no longer reset draft ownership; account/domain/organization/case changes remount the document state.
limitations: Component tests use mocked API transport and synthetic documents; backend regression tests use isolated HTTP/database fixtures. No live model or native-client acceptance.
No complete-suite rerun or backend rebuild in this frontend-only batch.
Frontend abort and suppression of late notifications do not roll back already completed server writes; direct bid execution may continue in its original request scope.
The parent LegalHub case-list refresh and cache ownership were read but not refactored or fully verified. Tests here pass cases directly to the two actual workbench components.
Total code lines increased by 43 after adding regression tests; business-source reduction is 26, not 95 (the new shared hook and client changes are counted).
No client restart, commit, push, or real user data migration.
nextCandidates: LegalHub repeats personal-case list/active-case synchronization and has scope-sensitive organization refreshes; review response ownership and the parent-provided case before consolidating.
Cross-entry local-model endpoint persistence remains a separate open audit item from prune42.
